correctness.rationale: A precisely defined conditional hazard yields a survival product by the chain rule. Exact adjacent swap gives difference abr(a-b)(r-1)/((a+c)(b+c)(a+b+c)) for a,b>0,c>=0 and 0<r<1, giving global strict sort extrema. Closed geometric suffix fractions and summable infinite-product tails prove positive ascending and exponentially decaying descending limits, including the claimed positive constants and relative error. Standalone exact Fraction script passed 144 swap cases, 36,522 permutation comparisons and 144 finite geometric identities; numerical asymptotics passed 54 checks. Limits follow from proof, not experiments.

originality.rationale: Across the inspected source methods, models and comparisons, the exact any-length all-permutation weighted survival extremum and exponential family separation were not found. The original 2014 model supplies the hazard; subsequent 2017 work supplies random-order averages, and 2018 work documents qualitative order effects under distinct knockout rules. Existing published network work does not itself imply the exact focal result; incomplete supplements and possible generic product-order inequalities are disclosed priority risks.
residual_risks: Generic mathematical ordering-of-suffix-products literature may already imply or state the exact exchange lemma under a different name.
The supplementary analytic survival derivation associated with Traveset et al. (2017) was not inspected in full; it may provide stronger or equivalent detail.
The full 2004 Memmott paper was not read; its abstract identifies degree ordering, not the claimed updated-weight survival objective.
This result only isolates a one-focal no-feedback process; full stochastic coextinction cascades can have different optimal primary-loss sequences.

value.rationale: The strict sorting criterion optimizes focal survival over all exogenously specified partner-extinction orders without simulation. The positive versus exponentially vanishing survival for identical geometric partner weights exposes a qualitative order sensitivity of the ecological renormalization mechanism, distinct from already-known general statement that some network extinction orders are worse. Fixed-total normalization eliminates this sensitivity, isolating its cause. The result is an exact motivated benchmark, not an empirical impact claim.
